overview: Finalize simulation coverage by implementing deterministic state compression for long-running campaigns and optimizing the endgame ascension logic. This batch focuses on reducing memory footprint for 5,500+ tick simulations and ensuring zero-latency state restoration for Monte Carlo validation.

tasks.title: Implement Deterministic State Compression for Long-Running Campaigns
tasks.architectural_spec: Use C++20 concepts to define a fixed-size, zero-heap compression scheme for simulation state. Implement a bit-packing algorithm for integer-based state variables (ticks, entity IDs, resource counts). Ensure all operations are constexpr-friendly where possible. The compressor must handle 5,500+ ticks with <1KB overhead per snapshot. No dynamic allocations during compression/decompression cycles.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: 1. Compression ratio > 85% for standard simulation states. 2. Decompression time < 1ms for 5,500-tick state. 3. Zero heap allocations during compression/decompression. 4. All unit tests pass with deterministic output.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Faster load times and reduced memory usage for long campaigns, enabling smoother gameplay on lower-end hardware.

tasks.title: Optimize Monte Carlo Validation Loop for Endgame States
tasks.architectural_spec: Refactor the Monte Carlo validation loop to use a fixed-size ring buffer for state snapshots. Implement a branchless comparison algorithm for state equivalence checks. Ensure the validator can process 16,500 footsteps in <10ms total. Use C++20 std::span for zero-copy access to state data. No virtual functions in the hot path.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: 1. Validation of 16,500 footsteps completes in <10ms. 2. Zero deadlocks detected in 100 consecutive runs. 3. Memory usage remains constant regardless of tick count. 4. All validation results are bitwise identical across runs.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Immediate feedback on simulation correctness, ensuring consistent game behavior across different hardware configurations.

tasks.title: Cache Endgame Ascension Events for Instant Replay
tasks.architectural_spec: Implement a static cache for the last 10 ascension events using C++20 std::array. Each event is a POD struct with fixed-size fields. Use a simple index-based lookup for O(1) access. Ensure the cache is thread-safe via atomic indices. No dynamic memory allocation. The cache must be serializable to a binary blob for quick restoration.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: 1. Cache hit rate > 95% for repeated ascension queries. 2. Lookup time < 100ns. 3. Thread-safe access verified with 4 concurrent readers. 4. Binary serialization size < 2KB for 10 events.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Instant access to endgame summaries and event logs, improving the user experience during campaign review.
